'''Robert Joshua Rubin''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|r|uː|b|ɪ|n}}; August 17, 1926 – January 18, 2008)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.geni.com/people/Robert-Rubin/6000000048234549590|title=Robert Joshua Rubin (1926 - 2008) - Genealogy}}</ref> was an American [[mathematician]] whose work involved modelling complex [[physical system]]s. He was married to astronomer [[Vera Rubin]].<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last=Sullivan |first=Patricia |date=February 5, 2008 |title=Robert J. Rubin, 81; Scientist Whose Work Combined Disciplines |url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/02/04/AR2008020403043.html |access-date=July 3, 2022 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Robert Joshua Rubin was born in New York state to Benjamin Rubin, an artist, and Bess, a stenographer.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Yeager |first=Ashley Jean |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sHOdEAAAQBAJ |title=Bright Galaxies, Dark Matter, and Beyond: The Life of Astronomer Vera Rubin |date=August 15, 2023 |publisher=MIT Press |isbn=978-0-262-54723-9 |page=34 |language=en}}</ref> While in elementary school, he became a serious tennis player, an activity in which he would remain active through his college years.<ref name=":0" />

Initially enrolled at Johns Hopkins University, Rubin's studies were interrupted by the advent of [[World War II]]. He enlisted in the Navy. After the war ended, the Navy sent him to study chemical engineering at Cornell University on the [[V-12 Navy College Training Program|V-12]] program,<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 17, 2021 |title=Meet Vera Rubin |url=https://airandspace.si.edu/stories/editorial/meet-vera-rubin |access-date=March 24, 2025 |website=National Air and Space Museum |language=en}}</ref> where he played on the tennis team<ref name=":0" /> and completed his B.S. in 1947. He became engaged to Vera Florence Cooper in late 1947 before returning to Cornell for graduate work in the spring of 1948.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 30, 1947 |title=Engagement Told |url=https://wikipedialibrary.wmflabs.org/?next_url=/ezproxy/r/ezp.2aHR0cHM6Ly9hY2Nlc3MubmV3c3BhcGVyYXJjaGl2ZS5jb20vdXMvd2FzaGluZ3Rvbi1kYy93YXNoaW5ndG9uL3dhc2hpbmd0b24tZXZlbmluZy1zdGFyLzE5NDcvMTEtMzAvcGFnZS03Mg-- |access-date=March 22, 2025 |website=Washington Evening Star Newspaper Archives |language=en}}</ref> 

Robert and Vera were married in July 1948 following her graduation from Vassar College.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 7, 1948 |title=Miss Cooper Bride |url=https://wikipedialibrary.wmflabs.org/?next_url=/ezproxy/r/ezp.2aHR0cHM6Ly9hY2Nlc3MubmV3c3BhcGVyYXJjaGl2ZS5jb20vdXMvd2FzaGluZ3Rvbi1kYy93YXNoaW5ndG9uL3dhc2hpbmd0b24tZGMtd2FzaGluZ3Rvbi1ldmVuaW5nLXN0YXIvMTk0OC8wNy0wNy9wYWdlLTI4 |access-date=March 22, 2025 |website=Washington Dc Washington Evening Star Newspaper Archives Page 28 |page=28 |language=en}}</ref>

He received his Ph.D. in chemistry from Cornell in 1951; his doctoral advisor was [[Peter Debye]].<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Following completion of his Ph.D., Rubin worked at the [[Applied Physics Laboratory|Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory]] in Washington until 1955, when he became a visiting assistant professor of physical chemistry at the University of Illinois.<ref name=":0" />

Returning to Washington in 1957, and he joined the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology|National Bureau of Standards]] (later the National Institute of Standards and Technology) as a physicist.  He also was on their tennis team.<ref name=":0" />

During the 1960s, his family spent summers in the West, where Rubin worked at Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico and at the National Bureau of Standards in Boulder, Colo.<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
From 1948 until his death in 2008, he was married to [[Vera Rubin]]. After many years in which Vera arranged her education and employment to follow his schedule, Rubin eventually prioritised Vera's travel for research and observing.<ref name=":0" />

Their four children include [[Judith Young (astronomer)|Judith Young]] (astronomer) and [[Karl Rubin]] (mathematician).<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Mitton |first1=Jacqueline |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HzQXEAAAQBAJ&q=Vera+Rubin:+A+Life |title=Vera Rubin: A Life |last2=Mitton |first2=Simon |date=February 11, 2021 |publisher=Harvard University Press |isbn=978-0-674-91919-8 |language=en}}</ref>

== Associations ==
Rubin was a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and also a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]].<ref name=":0" />
